lanes.invariant: nightlyStaleSeconds + sweepTimerSeconds + sweepAccuracySeconds <= nightlyPhaseWaitSeconds - nightlyPollSeconds (a crashed nightly claim is swept to its fail-closed verdict while the lane wrapper is still polling its per-phase wait)

notes.pairing: nightlyStaleSeconds is driver-process NIGHTLY_STALE_SECONDS (browser-nightly claims only — every other lane, including absent-lane legacy envelopes, sweeps at staleSeconds); nightlyPhaseWaitSeconds/nightlyPollSeconds are the installed browser-nightly launcher's PHASE_WAIT_SECONDS/POLL_SECONDS. The bound must ALSO stay above the longest legit nightly phase (vm guard 11400 s + seed prep) so a live phase is never swept mid-run. Corrupt-claim policy: a .running claim whose envelope is unreadable/unparseable is never guessed to be the unit lane — it is logged loudly as corrupt and sweeps at nightlyStaleSeconds (the longest bound), so possibly-live nightly work is never killed by a read failure; a stale corrupt unit claim lingering to 11700 s is visible and non-fatal (still fails closed, only later).
notes.acceptedRisk: browser-suite claims still sweep at staleSeconds=4500 while their vm guard is 5400 s: raising the suite bound would need a longer suite wrapper deadline (factory-suite DEADLINE_SECONDS=5580 caps the pairing at 4610). Real suite runs finish far below 4500 s; a pathological >4500 s run surfaces as a swept exit 3, red and re-runnable — recorded here for the owner rather than silently widened.

invariant: staleSeconds + sweepTimerSeconds + sweepAccuracySeconds <= deadlineSeconds - pollSeconds (a mid-job crash is swept to a fail-closed verdict the waiting wrapper still sees before its own deadline)

notes.pairing: staleSeconds is driver-process STALE_SECONDS; deadlineSeconds/pollSeconds are factory-validate DEADLINE_SECONDS/POLL_SECONDS; sweepTimerSeconds + sweepAccuracySeconds are the OnUnitInactiveSec/AccuracySec of lemcentre-factory-sweep.timer. verify-recovery.sh re-checks the invariant from the INSTALLED artifacts; lemfleet controller/factory_recovery_drill.py re-checks it from these sources (read via --lem-reader-ops).
notes.coordination: #279 (guest->host artifact channel) and #280 (heavy-test lease in the factory path) may adjust the guest/job time bounds; any change to deadlineSeconds must re-satisfy the invariant here and in the paired lemfleet drill before provisioning.
notes.why: 7200s stale sweep previously outlived the 5580s wrapper deadline, so a crashed claim surfaced as the wrapper's exit-5 timeout and the claim lingered until an unrelated spool write. 4500 + 900 + 60 = 5460 <= 5570 keeps the swept exit-3 verdict inside the wrapper's wait; the sweep timer guarantees the sweep runs without a new spool write.
